searchText: What is the plan for getPayloadV2 and blockValue: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/314/files Do we plan to deliver it before the withdrawals fork? We prototyped it, and thanks to that, CLs could test it. We would like to have this prototype in the codebase. However, there is a conflict between the current withdrawal work and having this prototype. For example, withdrawal hive tests will fail after adding blockValue to getPayloadV2. Of course, the blockValue PR is still in the draft, so hive tests are correct. Should we switch the prototype to getPayloadV3? If we want to rollout this change before Capella/Shanghai then blockValue and withdrawals should have `V2` and `V3` versions respectively Okay, the decision is most important because we will know what should be included in devnets and hive tests. If we decide, we will avoid the chaos with Engine API versioning. We have the following options: 1. Block value before Capella getPayloadV2 - blockValue, getPayloadV3 - blockValue + withdrawals 2. Block value as part of the Capella getPayloadV2 - blockValue + withdrawals 3. Block value after the Capella getPayloadV2 - withdrawals, getPayloadV3 - blockValue + withdrawals So in terms of API, the cleanest solution is number 2, but it means that we should adjust the spec and implementations. And hive tests for withdrawal devnets ASAP. 1 - We won't be able to deliver it much ahead of Shanghai, so it doesn't make sense. 3 - is fine, but it means that we will deliver blockValue later What do other teams think about it? <@755590043632140352> <@476250636548308992> <@792822129019584562> <@680234424037670912> and other CL devs, whats the current agreement of how one must submit the "`change-operations.json`" file contents to publish the BLS change that is generated by `ethdo`? We should be fine with that formal <@412614104222531604> <@476250636548308992> Curl is not good enough currently I understand that the signing would not be supported by prysm (or any other CL) , I'm only interested if the publishing is something that clients plan to do? The endpoint does not take a list ahh right Would be good if there would be more than just a single tool to generate the BLS change though, so one could verify that the signature is the same with different independent tools. Cc <@550420431744794624> How would prysm (CLs) verify the signature before broadcasting? It would use the headstate to verify the change object and its signature like all other operations Right, but that would be an online operation as far as I can tell. We would need to have at least 2, if not more ways to generate the signature offline, given a mnemonic. do you mean generating or verifying the signature here ? Prysm will not be able to generate it We might mean something else under verifying. I mean that two (or more tools) should give the same signature, and I should be able to verify offline that those two signatures are the same. (I know that CL teams don't wanna deal with this). They will just verify that the signature is a valid one. I honestly think you just need 1 tool to generate the signature. Having a second tool doesn't really add anything, if your signature is indeed invalid, the CL client will reject it immediately. For a particular message a signature can only be valid/invalid , so double checking this with another tool doesn't help It does, you want to have an independent, off-line check that you actually generated a signature for the validator that you wanted to generate it and not another one. Ethdo deals with accounts for example and allows you to have an HD-wallet, Jim could easily wake up one day thinking "I'm gonna play April's fool on Kraken and whenever they want to exit validator N, I'll give them a signature for validator N+1". Sure, they can check this by reading the JSON, but still. Having an EF-repo audited application handling the mnemonics would be more than desirable Agreed. <@758579010027782144>, my personal preference is for 2 as well, this reduces complexity and we can start testing soonish, probably we can raise this as a last minute adition to the ACD today? cc <@552133098075193354> , Engine API is already in the schedule https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/675#issuecomment-1342492255 In the event they generated the wrong signature, what exactly would you do ? It just gets rejected altogether as the signature doesn't match with the object. The same applies when signing validator exits, you could be signing the signature for the wrong key here. I am not against having multiple tools to be able to do this, just saying that the average user doesnt need more than 1 tool to generate their execution change signature you're always to the rescue 🙂 in the event they generated the right signature for a different validator you may be in trouble If I put my mnemonic into any tool, I would want to be able to offline verify that at least the two tools give the same signature, for the same validator. Maybe I'm not an average user? <https://www.reddit.com/r/ethstaker/comments/jrkbe2/my_checklist_to_create_and_verify_accounts_and/> Only 21 upvotes though (and one of them was mine, and I trust `ethdo` 🙂 ) Probably not lol I think at that time I used ethdo cause I didn't trust the `deposit-cli` 🙂 You do now? 🙂 You shouldn't trust anything what if I don't trust ethdo? What additional information would you need to be comfortable that the operation was as you intended it to be? the point is to check one with the other one, doesn't matter which. Nishant is arguing that you do this anyway on the client, I argue that users want to have reassurance before sending the message avg user will have to put their trust in a tool that will actually use their mnemonic and create a signature. This is exactly my point. even if this is completely secure, having a single point of failure for user experience is not optimal. If you decide to remove the repo and dissappear from the community we will have to start vouching some random fork. Having more than 1 option to put selected trust in is a key advantage. Hence why we also have multiple clients for el and cl. Same applies to other aspects of ethereum, I don't like the situation with BLST at all Oh, don't misunderstand me, its not personal, I just want diversification for tools to create specific features, same way we demand it from CLs and ELs. There is a difference between "valid" and "verified". Any op with a matching signature is valid, but unless it does what the user wants it to do it isn't verified. Two separate sources of the signature would make sense, in that it would be about the only way to verify that the operation really was what it said it was. But then we're in to explaining to users how to compare them, and would we need a third tool for that? Compare json? Totally, I'm happy to add information and/or process to make this clearer to users. diff a.json b.json ? 😄 That's probably beyond many users' ability already, though. Having seen people trying to put files in the right place over the past couple of years a lot of stakers aren't technical. I think having multiple tools to generate signatures is obviously a positive as it reduces dependence on any one single tool being a single point of failure. But for the average user, they will only feed their mnemonic to one tool. Anything more complex then that involving generating signatures with another tool and comparing,etc has a heavy UX burden. You could generate the change ops from two different tools, upload them to a website, and the website would broadcast them after verifying them against each other. Perhaps not a terrible way to go. Agree, average Joe will use a single tool. Also average Joe should be able to choose which tool he/she wants to use. One obvious way would be to put whatever the user said in the change op JSON, but to sign it for my fund-for-an-evil-hideout address. When it comes to broadcast, `ethdo` would just swap out the address before sending the data to the beacon node and hey presto I have enough for my evil hideout.) you will have to change the signature for that as well but yeah, users won't find out nobody would check the signature tho thats the whole point Yeah, `ethdo` is passed op saying "change validator X to credentials Y", `ethdo` signs "change validator X to credentials Z". The JSON will still look okay, but the signature won't verify if checked by a third party. Which is where the third party to check the signature comes in to play. (All this is assuming that I'm evil, which I hope isn't the case but totally appreciate that something this important shouldn't _rely_ on me not being evil.) So: two different sources to generate the operations, and for non-technical users something with the ability to independently verify them, makes sense. <@144468805697929216> <@340345049063882753> you guys have always strong opinions on API questions: would there be strong oposition to request the BLS changes pool endpoint **only** takes a list? that is if you want to submit a single change then you'd send a list with only one entry. It seems that it would make our life much easier and since ethdo already covers this and no other signing tool is available, it's a good point to decide this I have no opinion either way. Handling the error case of "m succeeded, (n-m) failed" with a list of n items is going to have to happen within `ethdo` anyway, so it makes no difference to me. Note that we have been down this road, however, so worth taking a look at the arguments there: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/275 Ahh thanks, hadn't noticed that people already were arguing this Hive tests doc for withdrawals: https://notes.ethereum.org/@marioevz/Withdrawals-hive-testing Yeah I’m a little frustrated that we have a clear use case and benefit for it to accept an array but are refusing to make life easy for users. excerpts.author: marekm3498
excerpts.content:
Okay, the decision is most important because we will know what should be included in devnets and hive tests. If we decide, we will avoid the chaos with Engine API versioning.

We have the following options:
1. Block value before Capella
getPayloadV2 - blockValue, getPayloadV3 - blockValue + withdrawals
2. Block value as part of the Capella
getPayloadV2 - blockValue + withdrawals
3. Block value after the Capella 
getPayloadV2 - withdrawals, getPayloadV3 - blockValue + withdrawals

So in terms of API, the cleanest solution is number 2, but it means that we should adjust the spec and implementations. And hive tests for withdrawal devnets ASAP.
1 - We won't be able to deliver it much ahead of Shanghai, so it doesn't make sense.
3 - is fine, but it means that we will deliver blockValue later

What do other teams think about it?

excerpts.author: jgm

There is a difference between "valid" and "verified".  Any op with a matching signature is valid, but unless it does what the user wants it to do it isn't verified.

Two separate sources of the signature would make sense, in that it would be about the only way to verify that the operation really was what it said it was.  But then we're in to explaining to users how to compare them, and would we need a third tool for that?

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
`ethdo` has the private key and is doing the signing.  All that happens is that in the code today where it signs `(validator index, new withdrawal credentials)` I swap out `new withdrawal credentials` for `evil withdrawal credentials generated by me`) and sign that instead.  The JSON will still look okay, but the signature won't verify if checked by a third party.  Which is where the third party to check the signature comes in to play.

(All this is assuming that I'm evil, which I hope isn't the case but totally appreciate that something this important shouldn't _rely_ on me not being evil.)

So: two different sources to generate the operations, and for non-technical users something with the ability to independently verify them, makes sense.

excerpts.author: jgm

I have no opinion either way.  Handling the error case of "m succeeded, (n-m) failed" with a list of n items is going to have to happen within `ethdo` anyway, so it makes no difference to me.

Note that we have been down this road, however, so worth taking a look at the arguments there: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/275
